artists.biography:
Richard Melville Hall (born September 11, 1965), better known by his stage name Moby, is an American singer-songwriter, musician, DJ and photographer. He is well known for his electronic music, vegan lifestyle, and support of animal rights. Moby has sold over 20 million albums worldwide.  AllMusic considers him "one of the most important dance music figures of the early 1990s, helping bring the music to a mainstream audience both in the UK and in America".
Moby gained attention in the early 1990s with his electronic dance music work, which experimented in the techno and breakbeat hardcore genres. With his fifth studio album, the electronica and house music-influenced Play, he gained international success. Originally released in mid-1999, the album sold 6,000 copies in its first week, and it re-entered the charts in early 2000 and became an unexpected hit, producing eight singles and selling over 10 million copies worldwide. Moby followed the album in 2002 with 18, which was also successful, selling over 5 million copies worldwide and receiving mostly positive reviews, though some criticized it for being too similar to Play.
His next major release, 2005's mostly upbeat Hotel was a stylistic departure, incorporating more alternative rock elements than previous albums, and received mixed reviews. It sold around 2 million copies worldwide. After 2008's dance-influenced Last Night (2008), he returned to the downtempo electronica of Play and 18 with 2009's mostly-ambient Wait for Me, finding higher critical acclaim and moderate sales, as well as 2011's Destroyed. Moby's latest album, Innocents, was released on October 1, 2013.
Moby has also co-written, produced, and remixed music for Michael Jackson, David Bowie, Daft Punk, Mylène Farmer, Brian Eno, Pet Shop Boys, Britney Spears, New Order, Public Enemy, Guns N' Roses, Metallica, Soundgarden, and others.

perplexity.description:
Moby's third studio album, Everything Is Wrong, was released in March 1995 by Mute and Elektra Records. The album is a landmark in Moby's discography, showcasing his ability to blend electronic music with rock influences, resulting in a dynamic and genre-defying sound. Recorded and mixed by Moby himself in his Manhattan apartment using modest equipment, the album features a mix of energetic techno tracks, ambient interludes, and experimental rock elements. Guest vocalists Rozz Morehead and Mimi Goese contribute to the album's diverse textures, further highlighting Moby's collaborative spirit and genre versatility.

Musically, Everything Is Wrong stands out for its eclectic range, from the driving beats of "Feeling So Real" to the introspective ambience of "Hymn" and the raw rock energy of "All That I Need Is to Be Loved." The album marked a significant evolution from Moby's earlier, more club-oriented work, establishing him as a serious and innovative artist in the electronic and alternative music scenes. Upon release, it received generally positive critical reception, with outlets like NME awarding it an 8/10, while commercial success was steady, eventually surpassing 180,000 copies sold in the United States by 2002. The album's original release year, 1995, places it at a pivotal moment in the development of electronic music, cementing Moby's reputation as a genre pioneer.
